topics.title: Fade in and out
topics.keywords: fade opacity see-through appear disappear ghost keyframes
topics.explain: opacity says how much of a tag you can see. 1 means all of it, 0 means none, and 0.5 is half, like a ghost. @keyframes makes a change called fade, and animation plays it. infinite alternate means it goes in and out forever.

code.text:
Now you see me

I am a ghost. You can see through me.

legend.means: plays fade, and it takes 2 seconds

files.name: my-page.html
files.code:
Now you see me

I am a ghost. You can see through me.

insert.text:
<style>
  @keyframes fade {
    from { opacity: 0; }
    to { opacity: 1; }
  }
  h1 { animation: fade 2s; }
</style>

topics.title: Hover effects
topics.keywords: hover grow lift shadow focus focus-visible button tab
topics.explain: Hover means the mouse is on a tag. Here each button does a trick on hover: one grows, one lifts up with a shadow, and one changes color. :focus-visible gives the same trick when you reach a button with the Tab key, so people without a mouse see it too.

code.text:
<style>
  button {
    font-size: 18px;
    padding: 10px 16px;
    margin: 12px;
    border: none;
    border-radius: 8px;
    background: skyblue;
    transition: all 0.3s;
  }
  .grow:hover, .grow:focus-visible {
    transform: scale(1.2);
  }
  .lift:hover, .lift:focus-visible {
    transform: translateY(-6px);
    box-shadow: 0 8px 10px gray;
  }
  .color:hover, .color:focus-visible {
    background: gold;
  }
</style>
<button class="grow">Grow</button>
<button class="lift">Lift</button>
<button class="color">Color</button>

legend.means: works when the mouse is on it
works when you reach it with the Tab key

topics.title: Moving by itself
topics.keywords: keyframes animation infinite alternate percent loop animate
topics.explain: @keyframes is a plan for a move, with a name you choose. 0% is the start, 50% is halfway and 100% is the end. animation gives the plan to a tag: its name, how long, how many times and which way. infinite means forever, and alternate means there and back again.

topics.explain: A spin turns a tag all the way round, from 0deg to 360deg. linear keeps the speed the same, so the spin never slows down. A pulse grows a little and gets small again, like a heartbeat.

topics.title: Wipe and reveal
topics.keywords: wipe reveal clip-path inset cut hide show curtain
topics.explain: clip-path cuts away part of a tag, so only the rest shows. inset has four numbers: top, right, bottom and left. inset(0 100% 0 0) cuts away all of it from the right, and inset(0 0 0 0) cuts nothing, so the tag shows like a curtain opening. Write each line twice, once with -webkit- in front, so it works on every Mac.

<style>
  @keyframes wipe {
    from {
      -webkit-clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0);
      clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0);
    }
    to {
      -webkit-clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0);
      clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0);
    }
  }
  h1 { animation: wipe 2s; }
</style>

topics.title: One after another
topics.keywords: stagger delay animation-delay wave order wait
topics.explain: animation-delay makes a tag wait before its animation starts. Give each tag a longer wait, and they move one after another, like a wave. 0.1s is a short wait, and 1s is a long one. The word both keeps a waiting tag at its first step, so it stays hidden until its turn comes.

topics.title: Less motion for some people
topics.keywords: prefers-reduced-motion reduce motion kind dizzy sick no-preference media
topics.explain: Some people feel dizzy or sick when things on a screen move a lot, so their Mac can ask for less motion. Put your animation lines inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { }. Then they play only when the Mac did not ask for less. It is a kind thing to do for everyone who visits your page.

code.text: I spin, unless your Mac asks for less motion.

    h1 { animation: fade 2s; }
  }
  @keyframes fade {
    from { opacity: 0; }
  }
</style>
